title: Needlepoint doorstop cover
subtitle: A basketweave tent stitch cover for a standard brick doorstop in four geometric bands
excerpt: A needlepoint cover for a standard house brick, worked in basketweave tent stitch in four horizontal geometric bands. The canvas wraps the top and four sides of the brick; the base is left open. Finished to fit a brick of 22 by 10 by 6.5 cm.
sourceNotes: Doorstop construction adapted from Weldon's Practical Needlework, canvaswork accessories (1890s). Geometric band arrangement synthesised from geometric canvaswork examples in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A standard house brick used as the weight inside a needlepoint doorstop cover. A standard UK brick measures approximately 22 by 10 by 6.5 cm.

heroPrompt: A needlepoint doorstop cover in geometric bands of navy and cream, propping open an interior door, close-up showing the stitch texture, natural light.

content.text: This doorstop cover wraps a standard house brick in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. The canvas is worked as a cross-shaped cut that folds up around the brick: a top panel flanked by four side panels. Four horizontal bands of geometric pattern in three colours run across the top and continue down the sides.

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas. Cut a cross-shaped piece: a central 114 by 52 hole top panel with 86 by 52 hole side panels on the two short ends and 52 by 34 hole panels on the two long sides. Cut the canvas 46 by 56 cm to allow full margins around the cross shape

content.text: Main: DMC 930 / Anchor 1035: dark antique blue
Accent: DMC 932 / Anchor 1033: light antique blue
Mount the full cross-shaped canvas on a large scroll frame. Work the top panel first with the frame, then reposition to complete each side panel.

Work the top panel first. Divide the 52-hole height into four horizontal bands: Band 1 (14 holes) in the main colour, Band 2 (8 holes) with alternating main and contrast squares, Band 3 (16 holes) in main, Band 4 (14 holes) with a row of contrast diamonds on main background.
The geometric bands use the same colour structure on all panels so the pattern is continuous when the canvas is folded up around the brick.
Complete all five panels (top plus four sides). Block by dampening and pinning square.

and overcast the corner seams with strong linen thread. Tuck the base margin under the brick. The base is left open for grip.
The same cross-shaped template with a Bargello wave on the top panel and continental tent stitch on the sides gives a more textured result.
